---
title: "Recipe 9 — Ban an offender manually: a CEL rule with `action: ban`"
---

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/engine/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/engine) · [`internal/operator/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/internal/operator) | Enforcement | medium | 5 min | policy + engine | ban, CEL, WAFPolicy, TR-195 |

### Problem

You watched one source hammer a route. You want to stop that source now.
You do not want to wait for a score. You want the stop to leave evidence
and to name the rule that wrote it.

### Solution

A rule pack carries one rule with `action: ban`. The matcher can say one
word: the path. The source stays on the wall as a would-ban record.

1. Write the rule pack. The action is `ban`; the match is narrow:

```yaml
rules:
  - id: OPS-MANUAL-01
    name: manual-ban
    description: stop the offender on the login route
    action: ban
    expression: |
      request.method == "POST" && path.matches("/v1/chat/*")
```

2. Ship it the way every rule ships: the ConfigMap + the `WAFPolicy` CR.
   The CR points at the pack; Recipe 2 owns that surface. Compile and
   apply. The gate compiles the pack; the CRD carries the bundle.

```bash
kubectl -n trishula apply -f rulepack-manual-ban.yaml
kubectl -n trishula apply -f wafpolicy-with-ban.yaml
```

3. Probe the route from the offender source. The response carries the
   decision, the rule id and the body:

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST "http://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions?q=x"
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Trishula-Decision: ban
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
X-Trishula-Rule: OPS-MANUAL-01

banned by OPS-MANUAL-01
```

4. Read the ban evidence. Start the engine with `--ban-evidence`, then
   read the JSONL line the match wrote:

```bash
kubectl -n trishula logs deploy/trishula-engine | tail -3
```

```text
would-ban 192.0.2.10 tier=manual-rule score=0 sig={Class:manual-rule Paths:[/v1/chat/completions]}
```

5. Lift the ban. Remove the rule from the pack and re-apply. The next
   bundle no longer names the rule, so the match disappears. The scored
   window for that source decays on its own clock.

### Discussion

`action: ban` folds with the response ladder as a block class on the
inside. The same action folds as a direct would-ban out the back. The record carries the
`manual-rule` tier and the signature (`class`, `paths`). The same record
reaches the enforcer the scored path uses; a deployed enforcer publishes
the kernel row the same way. The verdict signals name the rule: the
consult-signal test in [#252](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/252)
pins `verdict.action=ban`, `verdict.rules=OPS-MANUAL-01` and
`verdict.dos.sig`.

Keep the match narrow. `action: ban` never waits for a score; a wide
expression bans whole routes. The fail-open posture: a failed evidence
write stays logged; the block decision stands.
